title: ר' אלעזר בר יוסי בן חלפתא

paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar son of Yose ben Chalafta went to Alexandria, as related in Chelek, and to Rome with Shimon to annul persecution. Yose would not let his son accompany Shimon bar Yochai until he promised not to punish him en route. Rashi: he did punish him with croup; remembering the promise to his father, he prayed, and the illness left his mouth for a sailor’s. There a miracle: the demon ben Temalyon entered the king’s daughter. In Rashi’s account, Elazar cured her, was allowed to take anything from the treasury, and took and tore only the decree against Israel. There he saw Temple vessels, the curtain with bull-and-goat blood from Yom Kippur, and the high priest’s frontlet. Me'ilah 17b; Yoma 57a with Rashi; Sukkah 5a, “I saw in Rome”; Niddah, Haro'eh: he ruled in Rome. Yoma 67a: Yose says, “My son Elazar spoke with me”; Rashi: jokingly, about my words. Pesachim 117a: “My son Elazar says.” Kiddushin 39a: Elazar from Yose Dormaska, from Yose the Galilean, from Yochanan ben Nuri, from Eliezer the great. Tosefta Orlah: from Yose Dormaskit, from Yochanan ben Nuri, from Eliezer the great. He was in Yavneh with Yehudah bar Ilai; he and Yose bar Yehudah reported in the name of Zekharyah ben Hakkatzav. Yuchasin forgot him in the tannaim and baraita-tannaim order, listing him only among Yose’s sons in the chronological section. In Chananya son of Abbahu’s name—requires examination there.
